**South Boston** , formerly **Boyd's Ferry** ,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Boston,_Virginia#cite_note-4) is a town in [Halifax County, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax_County,_Virginia "Halifax County, Virginia"), United States. As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), South Boston had a population of 7,966.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Boston,_Virginia#cite_note-Census2020PLLede-5) It is the most populous town in Halifax County.

On December 8, 1796, the [Virginia General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_General_Assembly "Virginia General Assembly") authorized eight commissioners to establish at Boyd's Ferry on the south side of the [Dan River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_River_\(Virginia\) "Dan River \(Virginia\)") the town of South Boston, named for [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"), [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts"). Because this site proved vulnerable to flooding, it was eventually abandoned in favor of a new settlement on the north side. By the 1850s the [Richmond and Danville Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond_and_Danville_Railroad "Richmond and Danville Railroad") passed through South Boston, which eventually developed into an important market for brightleaf tobacco. In 1884 it was incorporated as a town; in 1960 it became an [independent city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_city "Independent city"); and in 1995 it made history by being the first city in Virginia to revert to town status and rejoined Halifax County.
Within the town limits [Berry Hill Plantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berry_Hill_Plantation "Berry Hill Plantation"), [E. L. Evans House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._L._Evans_House "E. L. Evans House"), [Reedy Creek Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reedy_Creek_Site "Reedy Creek Site"), [South Boston Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Boston_Historic_District "South Boston Historic District"), are listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Boston,_Virginia#cite_note-nris-7) [Fourqurean House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourqurean_House "Fourqurean House"), [Glennmary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glennmary "Glennmary"), [Glenwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenwood_\(South_Boston,_Virginia\) "Glenwood \(South Boston, Virginia\)"), [Tarover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarover "Tarover"), and [Seaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seaton_\(South_Boston,_Virginia\) "Seaton \(South Boston, Virginia\)") are nearby.
South Boston was home to the National Tobacco Festival (a typically three day annual festival held every fall) from its inception in 1935 to 1941, when it was suspended during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"). In 1948, the festival was moved to [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Virginia "Richmond, Virginia") when it outgrew the town. It was held in Richmond until 1984, when it was canceled due to rising production costs and decreased interest.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Boston,_Virginia#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Boston,_Virginia#cite_note-9) South Boston was the second largest producer of tobacco in the United States until the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression_in_the_United_States "Great Depression in the United States").
## Geography
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Boston,_Virginia&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]
South Boston is located south of the center of Halifax County at

[36°42′28″N 78°54′12″W﻿ / ﻿36.70778°N 78.90333°W﻿ / 36.70778; -78.90333](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=South_Boston,_Virginia&params=36_42_28_N_78_54_12_W_type:city) (36.707722, −78.903388).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Boston,_Virginia#cite_note-GR1-10) It is bordered to the south by the unincorporated community of [Riverdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale,_Halifax_County,_Virginia "Riverdale, Halifax County, Virginia"). [U.S. Route 501](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_501_in_Virginia "U.S. Route 501 in Virginia") passes through the center of the town, leading north 5 miles (8 km) to [Halifax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halifax,_Virginia "Halifax, Virginia"), the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat"), and south 23 miles (37 km) to [Roxboro, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roxboro,_North_Carolina "Roxboro, North Carolina"). [U.S. Route 360](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_360_in_Virginia "U.S. Route 360 in Virginia") crosses the southeastern corner of the town limits, leading northeast 37 miles (60 km) to [Keysville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keysville,_Virginia "Keysville, Virginia") and west 31 miles (50 km) to [Danville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danville,_Virginia "Danville, Virginia"). [U.S. Route 58](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_58_in_Virginia "U.S. Route 58 in Virginia") passes through the southernmost part of South Boston with US 360, leading west with it to Danville but running east 48 miles (77 km) to [South Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Hill,_Virginia "South Hill, Virginia").
According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), South Boston has a total area of 13.2 square miles (34.1 km2), of which 13.1 square miles (33.8 km2) are land and 0.1 square miles (0.3 km2), or 0.74%, are water.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Boston,_Virginia#cite_note-Census_2010-11) The [Dan River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_River_\(Virginia\) "Dan River \(Virginia\)"), a tributary of the [Roanoke River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roanoke_River "Roanoke River"), flows to the east along the southern edge of the town.

As of the census[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Boston,_Virginia#cite_note-GR2-2) of 2000, there were 8,491 people, 3,502 households, and 2,185 families residing in the town. The population density was 694.7 people per square mile (268.3/km2). There were 3,946 housing units at an average density of 322.8 per square mile (124.7/km2). The racial makeup of the town was 50.63% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_\(U.S._Census\) "White \(U.S. Census\)"), 47.25% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_\(U.S._Census\) "African American \(U.S. Census\)"), 0.21% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_\(U.S._Census\) "Native American \(U.S. Census\)"), 0.48% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_\(U.S._Census\) "Asian \(U.S. Census\)"), 0.51% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_\(United_States_Census\) "Race \(United States Census\)"), and 0.92% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_\(U.S._Census\) "Hispanic \(U.S. Census\)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_\(U.S._Census\) "Latino \(U.S. Census\)") of any race were 1.45% of the population.
There were 3,502 households, out of which 29.0% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 39.0% were married couples living together, 20.0% had a female householder with no husband present, and 37.6% were non-families. 34.9% of all households were made up of individuals, and 16.3% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.26 and the average family size was 2.90.
In the town, the population was spread out, with 23.7% under the age of 18, 6.7% from 18 to 24, 25.1% from 25 to 44, 23.9% from 45 to 64, and 20.6% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 41 years. For every 100 females, there were 79.1 males. For every 100 females aged 18 and over, there were 73.4 males.
The median income for a household in the town was $25,964, and the median income for a family was $34,848. Males had a median income of $28,212 versus $20,371 for females. The per capita income for the town was $15,872. About 15.3% of families and 20.4% of the population were below the poverty line, including 24.2% of those under age 18 and 23.9% of those age 65 or over.
